                    ### Question
                    A thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus strain has been isolated at a retirement home. Many of the elderly had been infected with this strain and are experiencing shingles. Which of the following would be the best antiviral agent to treat this population?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Acyclovir
opb. Famciclovir
opc. Ganciclovir
opd. Cidofovir
ope. Amantadine

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus (VZV) strains are resistant to acyclovir, making it ineffective for treating infections caused by this strain. Famciclovir, which is a prodrug that converts to an active form effective against VZV, is a suitable alternative and is supported by evidence indicating its efficacy against Human herpesvirus 3 (VZV). Ganciclovir is primarily used for cytomegalovirus (CMV) and is not effective for VZV, while cidofovir has limited efficacy against VZV and is not the first choice. Amantadine is not effective for VZV infections. Therefore, famciclovir is the best antiviral agent for treating shingles in this population.
